pages.label: Apple: SUBSCRIBED
pages.title: What does the App Store notification SUBSCRIBED mean?
pages.description: SUBSCRIBED means a customer subscribed to an auto-renewable subscription. Subtype INITIAL_BUY is the first time, RESUBSCRIBE a return. Grant access and record the purchase.
pages.answer: The App Store notification SUBSCRIBED means a customer subscribed to an auto-renewable subscription, for the first time or again.
facts: Sent by
The App Store server, to your notification URL
pages.definition: The customer subscribed to an auto-renewable subscription. The subtype says whether it is the first purchase or a resubscribe.
causes: Subtype `INITIAL_BUY`: the customer bought or got access through Family Sharing to a subscription in the group for the first time, including by redeeming an offer code.

Subtype `RESUBSCRIBE`: the customer resubscribed, or got access through Family Sharing, to the same subscription or another one in the same subscription group, including through a promotional, offer code or win-back offer.
To tell whether an offer was used, Apple says to check `offerType` in the decoded transaction (`JWSTransactionDecodedPayload`).
fixes: Verify the `signedPayload` with Apple's App Store Server Library (`SignedDataVerifier.verifyAndDecodeNotification`) before you act on anything in it.
Decode `signedTransactionInfo`, find the customer through your own account link (for example the `appAccountToken`) and grant the entitlement until `expiresDate`.
Treat `RESUBSCRIBE` as access again, not as a second first purchase, so your counts of new subscribers stay right.

Answer HTTP 200 (any code from 200 to 206) once you have stored the notification. Apple retries other answers five times, at 1, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours after the previous attempt, so make your handler safe to run twice (the payload carries a `notificationUUID`).
pages.mapping: RevenueDot verifies Apple's signature, checks the bundle ID, stores the notification and answers 200. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. `SUBSCRIBED` is one of the types that update the stored purchase from the signed transaction and renewal info. A chain RevenueDot has not stored before produces `INITIAL_PURCHASE`; a chain it already holds with a new period produces `RENEWAL`, because RevenueCat reports a lapsed customer who resubscribes as a renewal and RevenueDot copies that. The subtype is not used; the stored state is.

pages.label: Apple: DID_RENEW
pages.title: What does the App Store notification DID_RENEW mean?
pages.description: DID_RENEW means the subscription renewed for a new period. With subtype BILLING_RECOVERY an expired subscription that failed to renew now renewed. Extend access.
pages.answer: The App Store notification DID_RENEW means an auto-renewable subscription renewed successfully for a new period.
facts: Sent by
The App Store server, to your notification URL
pages.definition: The subscription renewed. With subtype BILLING_RECOVERY, a subscription that previously failed to renew has now renewed. With no subtype, an active subscription auto-renewed.
causes: Without a subtype, the active subscription auto-renewed for a new transaction period.
Subtype `BILLING_RECOVERY`: the expired subscription that had failed to renew has renewed after the billing retry.
Apple says to give the customer access to the subscription's content or service.
fixes: Verify the `signedPayload` with Apple's App Store Server Library (`SignedDataVerifier.verifyAndDecodeNotification`) before you act on anything in it.
Read the new `expiresDate` from `signedTransactionInfo` and extend access to it.
If you showed a billing warning, remove it when the subtype is `BILLING_RECOVERY`.

Answer HTTP 200 (any code from 200 to 206) once you have stored the notification. Apple retries other answers five times, at 1, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours after the previous attempt, so make your handler safe to run twice (the payload carries a `notificationUUID`).
pages.mapping: RevenueDot verifies Apple's signature, checks the bundle ID, stores the notification and answers 200. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. `DID_RENEW` clears the billing issue on the stored purchase (a type override in the server code) and applies the new transaction. A new period gives a `RENEWAL` event, with `is_trial_conversion: true` when the previous period was a free trial. Recovering a failed payment is reported as `RENEWAL`, never as `UNCANCELLATION`.

pages.label: Apple: DID_RENEW / BILLING_RECOVERY
pages.title: What does the App Store notification DID_RENEW with subtype BILLING_RECOVERY mean?
pages.description: DID_RENEW with subtype BILLING_RECOVERY means an expired subscription that failed to renew has renewed after billing retry. Restore access and remove billing warnings.
pages.answer: The App Store subtype BILLING_RECOVERY on DID_RENEW means a subscription that failed to renew has now renewed after the App Store retried billing.
facts: Sent by
The App Store server, to your notification URL
pages.definition: The expired subscription that previously failed to renew has successfully renewed.
causes: The renewal charge failed earlier and the subscription entered the billing retry period. Apple keeps retrying for up to 60 days, or until the customer fixes billing or cancels.
The customer updated their payment method, or the retry succeeded on its own.
If the subscription had a billing grace period and recovered inside it, the customer never lost access.
fixes: Verify the `signedPayload` with Apple's App Store Server Library (`SignedDataVerifier.verifyAndDecodeNotification`) before you act on anything in it.
Restore access, and extend it to the new `expiresDate`.
Remove any in-app message that asked the customer to fix their payment method.
Do not count this as a new subscriber: it is the same subscription, recovered.

Answer HTTP 200 (any code from 200 to 206) once you have stored the notification. Apple retries other answers five times, at 1, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours after the previous attempt, so make your handler safe to run twice (the payload carries a `notificationUUID`).
pages.mapping: RevenueDot verifies Apple's signature, checks the bundle ID, stores the notification and answers 200. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. The stored purchase loses its billing issue and takes the new period, so RevenueDot sends `RENEWAL` and no `UNCANCELLATION`: the diff code skips `UNCANCELLATION` when a renewal recovers a billing issue.

pages.label: Apple: DID_FAIL_TO_RENEW
pages.title: What does the App Store notification DID_FAIL_TO_RENEW mean?
pages.description: DID_FAIL_TO_RENEW means a renewal failed because of a billing issue and the subscription entered billing retry. With subtype GRACE_PERIOD keep access; otherwise stop it and ask for new billing details.
pages.answer: The App Store notification DID_FAIL_TO_RENEW means a subscription failed to renew because of a billing issue and entered the billing retry period.
facts: Sent by
The App Store server, to your notification URL
pages.definition: The subscription failed to renew due to a billing issue and entered billing retry. With subtype GRACE_PERIOD, keep serving the customer; with none, you can stop.
causes: The customer's payment method was declined, expired or otherwise could not be charged at renewal.
Subtype `GRACE_PERIOD`: Billing Grace Period is on for the app, so the customer keeps access while Apple retries. Apple says to continue to provide service.
With no subtype there is no grace period, and Apple says you can stop providing the subscription service. Apple keeps retrying billing for 60 days.
fixes: Verify the `signedPayload` with Apple's App Store Server Library (`SignedDataVerifier.verifyAndDecodeNotification`) before you act on anything in it.
Tell the customer there may be a problem with their billing information and link them to their payment settings.
With subtype `GRACE_PERIOD`, keep access until the grace period ends (the renewal info has `gracePeriodExpiresDate`); with no subtype, pause access.

Answer HTTP 200 (any code from 200 to 206) once you have stored the notification. Apple retries other answers five times, at 1, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours after the previous attempt, so make your handler safe to run twice (the payload carries a `notificationUUID`).

snippet.expect: ask the customer to fix billing

pages.mapping: RevenueDot verifies Apple's signature, checks the bundle ID, stores the notification and answers 200. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. A type override marks the stored purchase as having a billing issue. RevenueDot sends `BILLING_ISSUE` (its `grace_period_expiration_at_ms` carries the grace end when the renewal info has one) and, as RevenueCat does, a `CANCELLATION` with `cancel_reason: BILLING_ERROR`. When access finally ends, the scheduler sends `EXPIRATION` with `expiration_reason: BILLING_ERROR`.

pages.label: Apple: GRACE_PERIOD_EXPIRED
pages.title: What does the App Store notification GRACE_PERIOD_EXPIRED mean?
pages.description: GRACE_PERIOD_EXPIRED means the billing grace period ended without a renewal, so turn access off. The App Store keeps retrying billing for up to 60 days.
pages.answer: The App Store notification GRACE_PERIOD_EXPIRED means the billing grace period ended before the subscription renewed.
facts: Sent by
The App Store server, to your notification URL
pages.definition: The billing grace period ended without renewing the subscription, so you can turn off access to the service or content.
causes: A renewal failed, Billing Grace Period was on, and the customer did not fix their billing before the grace period ended.
Apple says grace periods last 3 or 6 days for weekly subscriptions and 3, 16 or 28 days for monthly and longer ones, and cannot be changed once assigned.
The subscription is still in billing retry. Apple continues for 60 days, until the customer fixes billing or cancels.
fixes: Verify the `signedPayload` with Apple's App Store Server Library (`SignedDataVerifier.verifyAndDecodeNotification`) before you act on anything in it.
Turn off access now, and keep a message that asks the customer to update their payment method.
Keep listening: a later `DID_RENEW` with subtype `BILLING_RECOVERY` means billing recovered, and `EXPIRED` with `BILLING_RETRY` means Apple gave up.

Answer HTTP 200 (any code from 200 to 206) once you have stored the notification. Apple retries other answers five times, at 1, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours after the previous attempt, so make your handler safe to run twice (the payload carries a `notificationUUID`).
pages.mapping: RevenueDot verifies Apple's signature, checks the bundle ID, stores the notification and answers 200. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. A type override keeps the billing issue on the stored purchase. Access ends when the grace period passes, and the scheduler then records `EXPIRATION` with `expiration_reason: BILLING_ERROR`. The notification itself adds no new event.

pages.label: Apple: DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_STATUS
pages.title: What does the App Store notification DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_STATUS mean?
pages.description: DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_STATUS means the customer turned auto-renew off (AUTO_RENEW_DISABLED) or on (AUTO_RENEW_ENABLED). Access continues to the end of the paid period.
pages.answer: The App Store notification DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_STATUS means the customer changed whether their subscription renews automatically.
facts: Sent by
The App Store server, to your notification URL
pages.definition: The customer changed the subscription's renewal status. AUTO_RENEW_ENABLED means auto-renew was turned on; AUTO_RENEW_DISABLED means it was turned off, by the customer or by the App Store after a refund request.
causes: Subtype `AUTO_RENEW_DISABLED`: the customer cancelled from the App Store Subscriptions page, or the App Store turned off auto-renew after the customer started a refund through your app's refund request API.
Subtype `AUTO_RENEW_ENABLED`: the customer subscribed again after cancelling, which turns auto-renew back on.
Apple also sends it without a subtype when the customer cancels after a price increase notice.
fixes: Verify the `signedPayload` with Apple's App Store Server Library (`SignedDataVerifier.verifyAndDecodeNotification`) before you act on anything in it.
Keep access until `expiresDate`: the customer paid for the period.
On `AUTO_RENEW_DISABLED`, start your win-back flow. Apple suggests this notification as one input for deciding who is eligible for a promotional offer.
On `AUTO_RENEW_ENABLED`, stop the win-back flow.

Answer HTTP 200 (any code from 200 to 206) once you have stored the notification. Apple retries other answers five times, at 1, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours after the previous attempt, so make your handler safe to run twice (the payload carries a `notificationUUID`).
pages.mapping: RevenueDot verifies Apple's signature, checks the bundle ID, stores the notification and answers 200. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. Type overrides set auto-renew from the subtype. Turning it off gives a `CANCELLATION` event with `cancel_reason: UNSUBSCRIBE` (or the store's reason, or `BILLING_ERROR` when a billing issue exists); turning it back on gives `UNCANCELLATION`. Access is not touched, so no `EXPIRATION` is sent until the period ends.

pages.label: Apple: DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF
pages.title: What does the App Store notification DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF mean?
pages.description: DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF means the customer changed their subscription plan. UPGRADE starts now, DOWNGRADE at the next renewal, and no subtype means they reverted a downgrade.
pages.answer: The App Store notification DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF means the customer switched to a different subscription plan in the same group.
facts: Sent by
The App Store server, to your notification URL
pages.definition: The customer changed their subscription plan. UPGRADE takes effect immediately, DOWNGRADE at the next renewal date, and an empty subtype means the customer reverted to the current plan, cancelling a downgrade.
causes: Subtype `UPGRADE`: the upgrade takes effect at once and starts a new billing period. Apple gives the customer a prorated refund for the unused part of the old period.
Subtype `DOWNGRADE`: the change takes effect at the next renewal date and does not affect the active plan. A cross-grade to a different duration counts as a downgrade.
No subtype: the customer changed the renewal preference back to the current plan, which cancels a scheduled downgrade.
fixes: Verify the `signedPayload` with Apple's App Store Server Library (`SignedDataVerifier.verifyAndDecodeNotification`) before you act on anything in it.
On `UPGRADE`, switch the entitlement now, to the product in the new transaction.
On `DOWNGRADE`, keep the current plan and note the product in `autoRenewProductId` of the renewal info as the plan from the next renewal.
With no subtype, clear the scheduled change.

Answer HTTP 200 (any code from 200 to 206) once you have stored the notification. Apple retries other answers five times, at 1, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours after the previous attempt, so make your handler safe to run twice (the payload carries a `notificationUUID`).
pages.mapping: RevenueDot verifies Apple's signature, checks the bundle ID, stores the notification and answers 200. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. The renewal info's `autoRenewProductId` is stored. A downgrade scheduled for the next renewal gives `PRODUCT_CHANGE` with `new_product_id` set to that product. An upgrade arrives as a transaction for the new product, which gives `PRODUCT_CHANGE` with `product_id` the old product, plus `RENEWAL` when the new product starts a new period.

pages.label: Apple: EXPIRED
pages.title: What does the App Store notification EXPIRED mean?
pages.description: EXPIRED means a subscription ended. The subtype says why: VOLUNTARY, BILLING_RETRY, PRICE_INCREASE or PRODUCT_NOT_FOR_SALE. Remove access and keep the reason for win-back.
pages.answer: The App Store notification EXPIRED means a subscription has expired and the customer should lose access.
facts: Sent by
The App Store server, to your notification URL
pages.definition: The subscription expired. The subtype gives the reason: VOLUNTARY, BILLING_RETRY, PRICE_INCREASE or PRODUCT_NOT_FOR_SALE. With no subtype it expired for another reason.
causes: `VOLUNTARY`: the customer turned off renewal and the period ended.
`BILLING_RETRY`: billing retry ended without a successful charge.
`PRICE_INCREASE`: the customer did not consent to a price increase that needs consent.
`PRODUCT_NOT_FOR_SALE`: the product was not available for purchase when the renewal was due. No subtype means some other reason.
fixes: Verify the `signedPayload` with Apple's App Store Server Library (`SignedDataVerifier.verifyAndDecodeNotification`) before you act on anything in it.
Remove access to the paid features and mark the subscription as ended.
Use the subtype to choose the win-back message: a payment problem needs a billing prompt, a voluntary cancel needs an offer.
Keep the customer's data; they can resubscribe, which arrives as `SUBSCRIBED` with subtype `RESUBSCRIBE`.

Answer HTTP 200 (any code from 200 to 206) once you have stored the notification. Apple retries other answers five times, at 1, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours after the previous attempt, so make your handler safe to run twice (the payload carries a `notificationUUID`).
pages.mapping: RevenueDot verifies Apple's signature, checks the bundle ID, stores the notification and answers 200. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. Type overrides set the stored state from the subtype: `VOLUNTARY` turns renewal off and clears any billing issue, `BILLING_RETRY` marks a billing issue, `PRICE_INCREASE` stores the cancel reason `PRICE_INCREASE`. The `EXPIRATION` webhook event is recorded by RevenueDot's scheduler once access, grace period included, has ended, with `expiration_reason` taken from the stored state.

pages.title: What does the App Store notification OFFER_REDEEMED mean?
pages.description: OFFER_REDEEMED means a customer with an active subscription redeemed an offer. Subtype UPGRADE applies now, DOWNGRADE at the next renewal, and no subtype is an offer on the same plan.
pages.answer: The App Store notification OFFER_REDEEMED means a customer with an active subscription redeemed a promotional offer or an offer code.
facts: Sent by
The App Store server, to your notification URL
pages.definition: A customer with an active subscription redeemed a subscription offer. UPGRADE applies at once, DOWNGRADE at the next renewal date, and no subtype means an offer on the current subscription.
causes: The customer redeemed a promotional offer or offer code while subscribed. First-time and returning subscribers redeeming an offer arrive as `SUBSCRIBED`, and offers on consumables or non-consumables as `ONE_TIME_CHARGE`.

pages.description: REFUND means the App Store refunded a purchase. Revoke what the customer got, using the revocation date and reason. Applies to consumables, non-consumables and subscriptions.

The App Store server, to your notification URL

causes: Apple approved a refund request, whether the customer asked through Apple support or through your app's refund request API.
The decoded transaction has `revocationDate` and `revocationReason`, and `originalTransactionId` and `productId` identify the purchase.
Apple's Get Refund History endpoint lists a customer's refunded transactions.

Revoke the access or the credited item for that transaction, effective at `revocationDate`.
Keep a record of the refund against the customer for support.
Only roll back what that transaction gave: a refund of an old renewal does not undo the current period.
